key_insight: Equivariant foundation MLIPs can be made both fast and accurate by using architectures and training strategies that scale to ultra-large datasets without sacrificing key physics symmetries.
engineering_relevance: These models can accelerate molecular dynamics and materials screening by delivering high-throughput inference and scalable training for practical, community-benchmark applications.
method: Evaluated NequIP and Allegro equivariant MLIP architectures as foundation potentials.
Implemented accelerations in the NequIP infrastructure to reduce training cost on ultra-large datasets.
Benchmarked accuracy and speed across materials discovery, thermal conductivity, and near-equilibrium mechanical/thermodynamic tasks.
evidence_signal: The paper reports strong scalability, leading inference speeds, and excellent accuracy across multiple community benchmarks, including large-dataset regimes.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on dataset diversity and consistent transition-metal energy-surface descriptions, so transfer to new chemical spaces still needs careful validation.
paper_title: Fast and Accurate Foundation Models for Equivariant Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
